You are an expert GPU and HPC software engineer working autonomously on a Linux machine with an NVIDIA RTX 4090.

# Port `tsr-prims` from CUDA to OpenMP target offload

`/app` contains `tsr-prims`, the device-wide parallel primitives library of the
Tessera engine: prefix scans, reductions, a 256-bin histogram, LSD radix sort,
a bitonic small-sort and stream compaction. It is written in CUDA. Without a
GPU it runs through a fiber-based CUDA emulator (`include/tsr/device/emu`,
`src/device/emu`). With `-DTSR_ENABLE_CUDA=ON` it compiles with nvcc.

Port the library to **OpenMP target offload** (clang 18, `-fopenmp`), keeping
its public API and its performance.

The machine has an NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), CUDA 12.8 (driver, nvcc, libdevice),
and clang 18 with the NVPTX and host offload plugins (`/usr/lib/llvm-18`).
`OMP_TARGET_OFFLOAD=MANDATORY` is set. Build the original with
`-DTSR_ENABLE_CUDA=ON` to measure the baseline you have to match.

## What the finished repository must look like

1. **No CUDA anywhere outside `tests/`.** Remove every `.cu`/`.cuh` file. Remove
   the CUDA language from CMake (no `enable_language(CUDA)`, `CUDAToolkit`,
   `cudart` or nvcc). Remove all CUDA syntax and runtime calls, and remove the
   emulator and its thread pool. Do not use vendor escape hatches: `ompx_*`,
   inline asm/PTX, or `__nvvm`/`__builtin_nvvm` builtins. Use portable OpenMP
   only. Comments are not checked.
2. **Every primitive computes on the device.** Each call to a primitive must launch
   at least one `target` region. The library may not compute results on the host.
   It may not use host algorithms (`std::sort`, `std::partial_sum`,
   `std::accumulate`, `std::reduce`, …) in `src/` or `include/`. A call may copy
   at most 64 bytes from the device to the host, which is enough to return a
   scalar such as `compact_indices`' count. Device memory is allocated with the
   OpenMP device memory API (`omp_target_alloc`), and pointers passed to
   primitives are device pointers.
3. **Same public API** (`include/tsr/prims/prims.h`, `include/tsr/device/*.h`):
   - Function names, template instantiations and argument order are unchanged.
     The only change: every `cudaStream_t` parameter becomes `tsr::Stream`, an
     opaque pointer type that accepts `nullptr`. Primitives may run
     synchronously.
   - `tsr::DeviceBuffer<T>` and `tsr::Arena` keep every public member, with the
     same `cudaStream_t` → `tsr::Stream` substitution. They also keep their
     semantics: move, shrink without reallocation, alignment and arena overflow
     blocks.
   - Errors throw `tsr::Error` exactly where the CUDA version does (invalid bit
     ranges, aliasing, oversize bitonic input, out-of-range downloads, …).
   - Results are bit-identical to the CUDA version. That includes sort stability
     and the overwrite semantics of `histogram256`. Float sums may differ only by
     reassociation.
4. **Build interface.** `cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++`
   must work with these options:
   - `TSR_OFFLOAD_ARCH`: GPU architecture, e.g. `sm_89`.
   - `TSR_OFFLOAD_TARGETS`: offload target triple, used when `TSR_OFFLOAD_ARCH`
     is empty, e.g. `x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`, the host-offload device.
   - `TSR_BUILD_TESTS` and `TSR_BUILD_APPS`.

   The library target stays `tsr_prims`. An executable that links `tsr_prims`
   and has no device code of its own must get everything it needs to offload,
   and must still be able to use C++ exceptions.
5. **Portable.** The same sources must be correct when offloading to the GPU
   and when offloading to the host device. Do not assume that the runtime grants
   the team size or thread count you ask for.

## How it is graded

`tests/` is replaced by a hidden suite. Your repository is then built from
scratch twice, for `TSR_OFFLOAD_ARCH=sm_89` and for
`TSR_OFFLOAD_TARGETS=x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`, with
`CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo`. The hidden suite contains:

- **Correctness tests** on both devices. They cover edge cases, golden
  checksums from the CUDA version, in-place operation, error paths and the
  memory utilities.
- **An offload probe** that counts the kernel launches and device-to-host bytes
  of every primitive call (rule 2).
- **A performance benchmark.** It times each case below at n = 2^26 against the
  original CUDA library on the same GPU in the same run. Each time is the median
  of 15 calls, and every timed call includes a 1-element download of its output.
  Your time must not exceed the given multiple of the CUDA time:

| case | max time / CUDA time |
|---|---|
| exclusive / inclusive scan, `uint32_t` | 1.30 |
| reduce (Sum, Max), `float` | 1.60 |
| `histogram256` | 1.30 |
| `radix_sort_pairs`, 44-bit `uint64_t` keys + `int32_t` values | 1.50 |
| `radix_sort_pairs`, 32-bit `uint32_t` keys + `uint32_t` values | 1.50 |
| `compact_indices` | 1.45 |

All gates must pass. A port that is correct but slow scores 0.

- The repository is in /app. Every command runs in a fresh subshell starting in /app: `cd` and exported
  variables do not persist (prefix commands, or write them to a file and `source` it).
- A command times out after 1800 s. Build with `ninja` / `cmake --build -j` and keep benchmark runs bounded.
- The machine has no network access and nobody will answer questions. Work until the task is completely

- Edit files with heredocs (`cat <<'EOF' > file`), `sed -i`, or small python scripts.
- When you are completely finished, submit by running exactly `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`
  on its own. After that you cannot continue. The state of /app at that point is graded as-is.

# Device sources (.cu) are compiled by nvcc when TSR_ENABLE_CUDA is ON and by
# the host C++ compiler against the emulated backend otherwise.
function(tsr_device_sources)
  if(TSR_ENABLE_CUDA)
    return()
  endif()
  foreach(src IN LISTS ARGN)
    # CMake passes "-x c++" for CXX sources with a non-C++ extension.
    set_source_files_properties(${src} PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CXX)
  endforeach()
endfunction()

function(tsr_target_warnings target)
  if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang")
    target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE
      $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-Wall -Wextra -Wno-unknown-pragmas -Wno-unused-parameter>)
  endif()
endfunction()
set(TSR_DEVICE_SOURCES
  device/error.cu
  device/memory.cu
  prims/scan.cu
  prims/reduce.cu
  prims/histogram.cu
  prims/radix_sort.cu
  prims/bitonic_sort.cu
  prims/compact.cu
)

set(TSR_HOST_SOURCES)

if(NOT TSR_ENABLE_CUDA)
  list(APPEND TSR_HOST_SOURCES
    device/emu/runtime.cpp
    device/emu/fiber_context.cpp
    device/emu/cuda_runtime.cpp
  )
endif()

tsr_device_sources(${TSR_DEVICE_SOURCES})

add_library(tsr_prims STATIC ${TSR_DEVICE_SOURCES} ${TSR_HOST_SOURCES})
target_include_directories(tsr_prims PUBLIC ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/include)
target_compile_features(tsr_prims PUBLIC cxx_std_20)
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(tsr_prims PUBLIC Threads::Threads)
tsr_target_warnings(tsr_prims)
if(TSR_ENABLE_CUDA)
  set_target_properties(tsr_prims PROPERTIES CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION OFF POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
  target_compile_options(tsr_prims PUBLIC $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:--expt-relaxed-constexpr --extended-lambda>)
endif()
tsr_device_sources(prims_bench.cu)
add_executable(prims_bench prims_bench.cu)
target_link_libraries(prims_bench PRIVATE tsr_prims)
tsr_target_warnings(prims_bench)
set(TSR_TEST_SOURCES
  test_main.cpp
  test_emu.cu
  test_prims.cu
)

set(TSR_TEST_DEVICE_SOURCES ${TSR_TEST_SOURCES})
list(FILTER TSR_TEST_DEVICE_SOURCES INCLUDE REGEX "\\.cu$")
tsr_device_sources(${TSR_TEST_DEVICE_SOURCES})

add_executable(tsr_tests ${TSR_TEST_SOURCES})
target_link_libraries(tsr_tests PRIVATE tsr_prims)
target_include_directories(tsr_tests PRIVATE ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/third_party/doctest ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR})
tsr_target_warnings(tsr_tests)

add_test(NAME tsr_tests COMMAND tsr_tests --no-intro --duration=false)
set_tests_properties(tsr_tests PROPERTIES ENVIRONMENT "TSR_EMU_WORKERS=4")

// Tessera - device-wide parallel primitives (host API).
//
// All functions enqueue work on `stream`; temporaries come from `arena` and
// stay valid until the arena is reset. Pointers are device pointers.
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "tsr/device/backend.h"
#include "tsr/device/memory.h"

namespace tsr::prims
{
// ---- scan -----------------------------------------------------------------
// out[i] = sum(in[0..i))  (exclusive) or sum(in[0..i]) (inclusive). In-place
// operation (in == out) is supported. Instantiated for uint32_t, int32_t,
// uint64_t, int64_t and float.
template<typename T>
void exclusive_scan(const T *in, T *out, std::size_t n, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream);

template<typename T>
void inclusive_scan(const T *in, T *out, std::size_t n, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream);

// Exclusive scan that also returns the grand total to the host (synchronizes).
template<typename T>
T exclusive_scan_total(const T *in, T *out, std::size_t n, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream);

// ---- reduce ---------------------------------------------------------------
enum class ReduceOp : std::uint8_t
{
    Sum,
    Max,
    Min,
};

// Reduces n values into *out (device pointer). Instantiated for float,
// uint32_t and int32_t. An empty input produces the operation's identity.
template<typename T>
void reduce(const T *in, std::size_t n, T *out, ReduceOp op, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream);

// ---- histogram ------------------------------------------------------------
constexpr std::uint32_t kHistogramBins = 256;

// hist[b] = number of i with bins[i] == b, for b < 256. Values >= 256 are
// ignored. hist must hold kHistogramBins counters; it is overwritten.
void histogram256(const std::uint32_t *bins, std::size_t n, std::uint32_t *hist, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream);

// ---- sorting --------------------------------------------------------------
// Stable LSD radix sort of (key, value) pairs on key bits [begin_bit, end_bit).
// Bits outside that range are ignored by the radix passes. Inputs are left
// untouched; results are written to keys_out / values_out. Instantiated for
// (uint64_t, int32_t), (uint32_t, uint32_t) and (uint32_t, int32_t).
template<typename K, typename V>
void radix_sort_pairs(
    const K *keys_in,
    K *keys_out,
    const V *values_in,
    V *values_out,
    std::size_t n,
    int begin_bit,
    int end_bit,
    Arena &arena,
    cudaStream_t stream
);

// Largest input handled by the single-block bitonic network.
constexpr std::size_t kBitonicMaxElements = 1024;

// In-block bitonic sort of up to kBitonicMaxElements pairs, ordered by
// (key, value). Same instantiations as radix_sort_pairs.
template<typename K, typename V>
void bitonic_sort_pairs(const K *keys_in, K *keys_out, const V *values_in, V *values_out, std::size_t n, cudaStream_t stream);

// Sorts pairs choosing the cheapest correct algorithm for n. Ordering is by
// key, then by original position (equivalently by value when values were
// emitted in increasing order).
template<typename K, typename V>
void sort_pairs(
    const K *keys_in,
    K *keys_out,
    const V *values_in,
    V *values_out,
    std::size_t n,
    int begin_bit,
    int end_bit,
    Arena &arena,
    cudaStream_t stream
);

// ---- compaction -----------------------------------------------------------
// Writes the indices i with flags[i] != 0 to out_indices in increasing order
// and returns how many there were (synchronizes).

//
// DeviceBuffer<T>  RAII owner of a typed device allocation.
// Arena            bump allocator for per-frame temporaries (sort scratch,
//                  scan carries, intersection lists). Allocations are 256-byte
//                  aligned and released all at once by reset().
#pragma once

template<typename T>
class DeviceBuffer
{
public:
    DeviceBuffer() = default;
    explicit DeviceBuffer(std::size_t count) { resize(count); }
    DeviceBuffer(const DeviceBuffer &)            = delete;
    DeviceBuffer &operator=(const DeviceBuffer &) = delete;
    DeviceBuffer(DeviceBuffer &&other) noexcept { swap(other); }
    DeviceBuffer &operator=(DeviceBuffer &&other) noexcept
    {
        if(this != &other)
        {
            release();
            swap(other);
        }
        return *this;
    }
    ~DeviceBuffer() { release(); }

    // Reallocates only when growing; contents are not preserved.
    void resize(std::size_t count)
    {
        if(count <= capacity_)
        {
            size_ = count;
            return;
        }
        release();
        if(count > 0)
        {
            TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(reinterpret_cast<void **>(&data_), count * sizeof(T)));
        }
        size_     = count;
        capacity_ = count;
    }

    void release()
    {
        if(data_ != nullptr)
        {
            cudaFree(data_);
        }
        data_     = nullptr;
        size_     = 0;
        capacity_ = 0;
    }

    void zero(cudaStream_t stream = nullptr)
    {
        if(size_ > 0)
        {
            TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemsetAsync(data_, 0, size_ * sizeof(T), stream));
        }
    }

    void upload(const T *host, std::size_t count, cudaStream_t stream = nullptr)
    {
        resize(count);
        if(count > 0)
        {
            TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(data_, host, count * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream));
        }
    }

    void upload(const std::vector<T> &host, cudaStream_t stream = nullptr) { upload(host.data(), host.size(), stream); }

    void download(T *host, std::size_t count, cudaStream_t stream = nullptr) const
    {
        TSR_CHECK(count <= size_, "download of " << count << " elements from a buffer of " << size_);
        if(count > 0)
        {
            TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(host, data_, count * sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, stream));
            TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
        }
    }

    [[nodiscard]] std::vector<T> to_host(cudaStream_t stream = nullptr) const
    {
        std::vector<T> out(size_);
        download(out.data(), size_, stream);
        return out;
    }

    [[nodiscard]] T *data() noexcept { return data_; }
    [[nodiscard]] const T *data() const noexcept { return data_; }
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t size() const noexcept { return size_; }
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t bytes() const noexcept { return size_ * sizeof(T); }
    [[nodiscard]] bool empty() const noexcept { return size_ == 0; }

    void swap(DeviceBuffer &other) noexcept
    {
        std::swap(data_, other.data_);
        std::swap(size_, other.size_);
        std::swap(capacity_, other.capacity_);
    }

private:
    T *data_              = nullptr;
    std::size_t size_     = 0;
    std::size_t capacity_ = 0;
};

class Arena
{
public:
    static constexpr std::size_t kAlignment = 256;

    Arena() = default;
    explicit Arena(std::size_t initial_bytes) { reserve(initial_bytes); }
    Arena(const Arena &)            = delete;
    Arena &operator=(const Arena &) = delete;

    // Discards every allocation. Memory is kept for reuse; if the previous
    // frame overflowed into extra chunks they are coalesced into one block.
    void reset();

    void reserve(std::size_t bytes);

    void *allocate_bytes(std::size_t bytes);

    template<typename T>
    T *allocate(std::size_t count)
    {
        return static_cast<T *>(allocate_bytes(count * sizeof(T)));
    }

    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t used() const noexcept { return used_; }
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t high_water() const noexcept { return high_water_; }
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t capacity() const noexcept;

private:
    static std::size_t align_up(std::size_t v) { return (v + kAlignment - 1) / kAlignment * kAlignment; }

    DeviceBuffer<std::uint8_t> main_;
    std::vector<DeviceBuffer<std::uint8_t>> overflow_;
    std::size_t offset_     = 0;
    std::size_t used_       = 0;
    std::size_t high_water_ = 0;
};

// Tessera - device-wide prefix sums.
//
// Hierarchical scan after the cuda-samples "scan" sample (BSD-3-Clause):
//   1. scan_tiles_kernel     scans 1024-element tiles (256 threads x 4 items)
//                            and records each tile's total
//   2. (recursion)           exclusive scan of the tile totals
//   3. uniform_add_kernel    adds each tile's offset to its elements
// Unlike the sample, lengths need not be powers of two: the tail tile is
// zero-padded on load and masked on store.
#include "tsr/prims/block.cuh"
#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"

namespace tsr::prims
{
namespace
{
constexpr unsigned kScanThreads = 256;
constexpr unsigned kScanItems   = 4;
constexpr unsigned kScanTile    = kScanThreads * kScanItems;

// `in` and `out` may alias (in-place scans), so they are not __restrict__.
template<typename T>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(kScanThreads)
    scan_tiles_kernel(const T *in, T *out, T *__restrict__ tile_totals, std::uint64_t n, bool inclusive)
{
    cg::thread_block cta = cg::this_thread_block();
    __shared__ T s_data[2 * kScanThreads];

    const std::uint64_t base = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * kScanTile + threadIdx.x * kScanItems;
    T items[kScanItems];
    T original[kScanItems];
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned k = 0; k < kScanItems; ++k)
    {
        items[k]    = base + k < n ? in[base + k] : T(0);
        original[k] = items[k];
    }

    T tile_total;
    scan4_exclusive(items, s_data, kScanThreads, cta, tile_total);

    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned k = 0; k < kScanItems; ++k)
    {
        if(base + k < n)
        {
            out[base + k] = inclusive ? items[k] + original[k] : items[k];
        }
    }
    if(tile_totals != nullptr && threadIdx.x == 0)
    {
        tile_totals[blockIdx.x] = tile_total;
    }
}

template<typename T>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(kScanThreads)
    uniform_add_kernel(T *__restrict__ data, const T *__restrict__ tile_offsets, std::uint64_t n)
{
    cg::thread_block cta = cg::this_thread_block();
    __shared__ T buf;
    if(threadIdx.x == 0)
    {
        buf = tile_offsets[blockIdx.x];
    }
    cg::sync(cta);

    const std::uint64_t base = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * kScanTile + threadIdx.x * kScanItems;
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned k = 0; k < kScanItems; ++k)
    {
        if(base + k < n)
        {
            data[base + k] += buf;
        }
    }
}

template<typename T>
void scan_impl(const T *in, T *out, std::size_t n, bool inclusive, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    if(n == 0)
    {
        return;
    }
    const std::uint64_t tiles = div_round_up<std::uint64_t>(n, kScanTile);
    TSR_CHECK(tiles <= 0x7fffffffu, "scan of " << n << " elements exceeds the grid limit");
    T *tile_totals = tiles > 1 ? arena.allocate<T>(tiles) : nullptr;

    launch(
        scan_tiles_kernel<T>,
        LaunchConfig{dim3(static_cast<unsigned>(tiles)), dim3(kScanThreads), 0, stream},
        in,
        out,
        tile_totals,
        static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n),
        inclusive
    );
    if(tiles > 1)
    {
        scan_impl(tile_totals, tile_totals, tiles, false, arena, stream);
        launch(
            uniform_add_kernel<T>,
            LaunchConfig{dim3(static_cast<unsigned>(tiles)), dim3(kScanThreads), 0, stream},
            out,
            tile_totals,
            static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n)
        );
    }
}
} // namespace

template<typename T>
void exclusive_scan(const T *in, T *out, std::size_t n, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    scan_impl(in, out, n, false, arena, stream);
}

template<typename T>
void inclusive_scan(const T *in, T *out, std::size_t n, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    scan_impl(in, out, n, true, arena, stream);
}

template<typename T>
T exclusive_scan_total(const T *in, T *out, std::size_t n, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    if(n == 0)
    {
        return T(0);
    }
    // Read the last input before the scan: with in == out it is overwritten.
    T last_in = T(0);
    TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(&last_in, in + n - 1, sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, stream));
    TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    scan_impl(in, out, n, false, arena, stream);
    T last_out = T(0);
    TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(&last_out, out + n - 1, sizeof(T), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, stream));
    TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(stream));
    return last_out + last_in;
}

#define TSR_INSTANTIATE_SCAN(T)                                                                    \
    template void exclusive_scan<T>(const T *, T *, std::size_t, Arena &, cudaStream_t);           \
    template void inclusive_scan<T>(const T *, T *, std::size_t, Arena &, cudaStream_t);           \
    template T exclusive_scan_total<T>(const T *, T *, std::size_t, Arena &, cudaStream_t);

TSR_INSTANTIATE_SCAN(std::uint32_t)
TSR_INSTANTIATE_SCAN(std::int32_t)
TSR_INSTANTIATE_SCAN(std::uint64_t)
TSR_INSTANTIATE_SCAN(std::int64_t)
TSR_INSTANTIATE_SCAN(float)

#undef TSR_INSTANTIATE_SCAN

// Tessera - device memory ownership.
#include "tsr/device/memory.h"

namespace tsr
{
void Arena::reserve(std::size_t bytes)
{
    bytes = align_up(bytes);
    if(bytes > main_.size())
    {
        TSR_CHECK(offset_ == 0 && overflow_.empty(), "Arena::reserve called while allocations are live");
        main_.resize(bytes);
    }
}

void Arena::reset()
{
    if(!overflow_.empty())
    {
        // Grow the main block so the next frame fits without overflowing.
        const std::size_t want = align_up(high_water_);
        overflow_.clear();
        main_.release();
        main_.resize(want);
    }
    offset_ = 0;
    used_   = 0;
}

void *Arena::allocate_bytes(std::size_t bytes)
{
    const std::size_t aligned = align_up(bytes == 0 ? 1 : bytes);
    used_                    += aligned;
    if(used_ > high_water_)
    {
        high_water_ = used_;
    }
    if(offset_ + aligned <= main_.size())
    {
        void *p  = main_.data() + offset_;
        offset_ += aligned;
        return p;
    }
    overflow_.emplace_back(aligned);
    return overflow_.back().data();
}

std::size_t Arena::capacity() const noexcept
{
    std::size_t total = main_.size();
    for(const auto &b : overflow_)
    {
        total += b.size();
    }
    return total;
}

// Tessera - device-wide reductions.
//
// Two-pass reduction modelled on reduce7 from the cuda-samples "reduction"
// sample (BSD-3-Clause): a grid-stride loop accumulates several elements per
// thread, warps reduce with shuffles and one warp folds the per-warp partials.
// The first pass writes one partial per block, the second pass runs a single
// block over the partials.
//
// Differences from the sample: the operation is a template parameter, and the
// final warp reduction runs over the full warp with identity padding instead
// of a ballot-derived partial mask (shuffling from lanes outside the mask is
// undefined behaviour that the sample relies on).
#include <algorithm>

#include "tsr/prims/block.cuh"
#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"

namespace tsr::prims
{
namespace
{
constexpr unsigned kReduceThreads = 256;
constexpr unsigned kMaxPartials   = 512;

template<typename T, typename Op, bool kTwoPerThread>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(kReduceThreads)
    reduce_kernel(const T *__restrict__ in, T *__restrict__ out, std::uint64_t n)
{
    __shared__ T s_warp[kReduceThreads / kWarpSize];
    const Op op{};
    T acc = Op::identity();

    if constexpr(kTwoPerThread)
    {
        // Each iteration consumes two blocks' worth of elements.
        std::uint64_t i               = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * kReduceThreads * 2 + threadIdx.x;
        const std::uint64_t grid_size = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(kReduceThreads) * 2 * gridDim.x;
        while(i < n)
        {
            acc = op(acc, in[i]);
            if(i + kReduceThreads < n)
            {
                acc = op(acc, in[i + kReduceThreads]);
            }
            i += grid_size;
        }
    }
    else
    {
        std::uint64_t i               = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * kReduceThreads + threadIdx.x;
        const std::uint64_t grid_size = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(kReduceThreads) * gridDim.x;
        while(i < n)
        {
            acc = op(acc, in[i]);
            i  += grid_size;
        }
    }

    acc = block_reduce<kReduceThreads>(acc, op, s_warp);
    if(threadIdx.x == 0)
    {
        out[blockIdx.x] = acc;
    }
}

template<typename T, typename Op>
void reduce_with(const T *in, std::size_t n, T *out, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    // Enough blocks to keep every worker busy, few enough that the second
    // pass is a single block.
    const unsigned blocks = static_cast<unsigned>(std::clamp<std::size_t>(div_round_up<std::size_t>(n, kReduceThreads * 8), 1, kMaxPartials));
    T *partials           = arena.allocate<T>(blocks);
    const bool pow2       = n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0;
    if(pow2)
    {
        launch(reduce_kernel<T, Op, true>, LaunchConfig{dim3(blocks), dim3(kReduceThreads), 0, stream}, in, partials, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n));
    }
    else
    {
        launch(reduce_kernel<T, Op, false>, LaunchConfig{dim3(blocks), dim3(kReduceThreads), 0, stream}, in, partials, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n));
    }
    launch(reduce_kernel<T, Op, false>, LaunchConfig{dim3(1), dim3(kReduceThreads), 0, stream}, partials, out, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blocks));
}
} // namespace

template<typename T>
void reduce(const T *in, std::size_t n, T *out, ReduceOp op, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    switch(op)
    {
    case ReduceOp::Sum: reduce_with<T, SumOp<T>>(in, n, out, arena, stream); break;
    case ReduceOp::Max: reduce_with<T, MaxOp<T>>(in, n, out, arena, stream); break;
    case ReduceOp::Min: reduce_with<T, MinOp<T>>(in, n, out, arena, stream); break;
    }
}

template void reduce<float>(const float *, std::size_t, float *, ReduceOp, Arena &, cudaStream_t);
template void reduce<std::uint32_t>(const std::uint32_t *, std::size_t, std::uint32_t *, ReduceOp, Arena &, cudaStream_t);
template void reduce<std::int32_t>(const std::int32_t *, std::size_t, std::int32_t *, ReduceOp, Arena &, cudaStream_t);
} // namespace tsr::prims
// Tessera - 256-bin histogram.
//
// After histogram256 from the cuda-samples "histogram" sample (BSD-3-Clause):
// every warp owns a private sub-histogram in shared memory to spread atomic
// contention, the sub-histograms are merged per block into partial
// histograms, and a second kernel (one block per bin) sums the partials.
// The input here is one bin index per element instead of four packed bytes.
#include <algorithm>

#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"
#include "tsr/prims/warp.cuh"

namespace tsr::prims
{
namespace
{
constexpr unsigned kHistWarps       = 6;
constexpr unsigned kHistThreads     = kHistWarps * kWarpSize;
constexpr unsigned kHistBlockMemory = kHistWarps * kHistogramBins;
constexpr unsigned kMaxPartials     = 240;
constexpr unsigned kMergeThreads    = 256;

__global__ void __launch_bounds__(kHistThreads)
    histogram256_kernel(std::uint32_t *__restrict__ partials, const std::uint32_t *__restrict__ bins, std::uint64_t n)
{
    cg::thread_block cta = cg::this_thread_block();
    __shared__ std::uint32_t s_hist[kHistBlockMemory];
    std::uint32_t *s_warp_hist = s_hist + warp_id() * kHistogramBins;

    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned i = 0; i < kHistBlockMemory / kHistThreads; ++i)
    {
        s_hist[threadIdx.x + i * kHistThreads] = 0;
    }
    cg::sync(cta);

    const std::uint64_t stride = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockDim.x) * gridDim.x;
    for(std::uint64_t pos = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; pos < n; pos += stride)
    {
        const std::uint32_t b = bins[pos];
        if(b < kHistogramBins)
        {
            atomicAdd(s_warp_hist + b, 1u);
        }
    }
    cg::sync(cta);

    for(unsigned bin = threadIdx.x; bin < kHistogramBins; bin += kHistThreads)
    {
        std::uint32_t sum = 0;
        for(unsigned w = 0; w < kHistWarps; ++w)
        {
            sum += s_hist[bin + w * kHistogramBins];
        }
        partials[blockIdx.x * kHistogramBins + bin] = sum;
    }
}

// One block per bin: each block adds up the same bin from every partial.
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(kMergeThreads)
    merge_histogram256_kernel(std::uint32_t *__restrict__ hist, const std::uint32_t *__restrict__ partials, unsigned partial_count)
{
    cg::thread_block cta = cg::this_thread_block();
    std::uint32_t sum    = 0;
    for(unsigned i = threadIdx.x; i < partial_count; i += kMergeThreads)
    {
        sum += partials[blockIdx.x + i * kHistogramBins];
    }

    __shared__ std::uint32_t data[kMergeThreads];
    data[threadIdx.x] = sum;
    for(unsigned stride = kMergeThreads / 2; stride > 0; stride >>= 1)
    {
        cg::sync(cta);
        if(threadIdx.x < stride)
        {
            data[threadIdx.x] += data[threadIdx.x + stride];
        }
    }
    if(threadIdx.x == 0)
    {
        hist[blockIdx.x] = data[0];
    }
}
} // namespace

void histogram256(const std::uint32_t *bins, std::size_t n, std::uint32_t *hist, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    const unsigned partial_count = static_cast<unsigned>(std::clamp<std::size_t>(div_round_up<std::size_t>(n, kHistThreads * 16), 1, kMaxPartials));
    std::uint32_t *partials      = arena.allocate<std::uint32_t>(static_cast<std::size_t>(partial_count) * kHistogramBins);
    launch(histogram256_kernel, LaunchConfig{dim3(partial_count), dim3(kHistThreads), 0, stream}, partials, bins, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n));
    launch(merge_histogram256_kernel, LaunchConfig{dim3(kHistogramBins), dim3(kMergeThreads), 0, stream}, hist, partials, partial_count);
}
} // namespace tsr::prims

// Tessera - stable LSD radix sort of key/value pairs.
//
// Each pass sorts on a 4-bit digit in three steps:
//   upsweep    per-tile digit counts, stored digit-major so that one exclusive
//              scan turns them into global scatter offsets
//   scan       prims::exclusive_scan over 16 * num_tiles counters
//   downsweep  ranks every key within its tile and scatters it
//
// Ranking is stable without block-wide scans: a tile is split into one
// contiguous 128-key chunk per warp, chunks are processed 32 keys at a time in
// order, and lanes holding equal digits are found with one ballot per digit
// bit. Per-warp running digit counts live in shared memory and are folded
// across warps once per tile.
#include <algorithm>

#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"
#include "tsr/prims/warp.cuh"

namespace tsr::prims
{
namespace
{
constexpr int kRadixBits          = 4;
constexpr unsigned kRadixDigits   = 1u << kRadixBits;
constexpr unsigned kSortThreads   = 256;
constexpr unsigned kSortItems     = 4;
constexpr unsigned kSortWarps     = kSortThreads / kWarpSize;
constexpr unsigned kSortWarpChunk = kWarpSize * kSortItems;
constexpr unsigned kSortTile      = kSortThreads * kSortItems;

template<typename K>
TSR_DI unsigned digit_of(K key, int shift, unsigned digit_mask)
{
    return static_cast<unsigned>(key >> shift) & digit_mask;
}

template<typename K>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(kSortThreads) radix_upsweep_kernel(
    const K *__restrict__ keys,
    std::uint64_t n,
    int shift,
    unsigned digit_mask,
    std::uint32_t *__restrict__ counts, // [kRadixDigits][num_tiles]
    unsigned num_tiles
)
{
    __shared__ std::uint32_t s_counts[kRadixDigits];
    if(threadIdx.x < kRadixDigits)
    {
        s_counts[threadIdx.x] = 0;
    }
    __syncthreads();

    const std::uint64_t base = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * kSortTile;
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned k = 0; k < kSortItems; ++k)
    {
        const std::uint64_t idx = base + k * kSortThreads + threadIdx.x;
        if(idx < n)
        {
            atomicAdd(&s_counts[digit_of(keys[idx], shift, digit_mask)], 1u);
        }
    }
    __syncthreads();

    if(threadIdx.x < kRadixDigits)
    {
        counts[threadIdx.x * num_tiles + blockIdx.x] = s_counts[threadIdx.x];
    }
}

template<typename K, typename V>
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(kSortThreads) radix_downsweep_kernel(
    const K *__restrict__ keys_in,
    K *__restrict__ keys_out,
    const V *__restrict__ values_in,
    V *__restrict__ values_out,
    std::uint64_t n,
    int shift,
    unsigned digit_mask,
    const std::uint32_t *__restrict__ offsets, // exclusive scan of the upsweep counts
    unsigned num_tiles
)
{
    __shared__ std::uint32_t s_warp_counts[kSortWarps][kRadixDigits];
    const unsigned lane = lane_id();
    const unsigned warp = warp_id();
    if(lane < kRadixDigits)
    {
        s_warp_counts[warp][lane] = 0;
    }
    __syncwarp();

    const std::uint64_t chunk = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * kSortTile + warp * kSortWarpChunk;
    K keys[kSortItems];
    V values[kSortItems];
    unsigned digits[kSortItems];
    std::uint32_t ranks[kSortItems];
    bool valid[kSortItems];

    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned k = 0; k < kSortItems; ++k)
    {
        const std::uint64_t idx = chunk + k * kWarpSize + lane;
        valid[k]                = idx < n;
        digits[k]               = 0;
        ranks[k]                = 0;
        if(valid[k])
        {
            keys[k]   = keys_in[idx];
            values[k] = values_in[idx];
            digits[k] = digit_of(keys[k], shift, digit_mask);
        }

        const unsigned peers     = warp_match_label<kRadixBits>(digits[k], valid[k]);
        std::uint32_t warp_count = 0;
        if(valid[k])
        {
            warp_count = s_warp_counts[warp][digits[k]];
            ranks[k]   = warp_count + static_cast<std::uint32_t>(__popc(peers & lanemask_lt()));
        }
        __syncwarp();
        // The lowest lane of each peer group advances the group's counter.
        if(valid[k] && lane == static_cast<unsigned>(__ffs(static_cast<int>(peers)) - 1))
        {
            s_warp_counts[warp][digits[k]] = warp_count + static_cast<std::uint32_t>(__popc(peers));
        }
        __syncwarp();
    }
    __syncthreads();

    // Exclusive scan across warps for each digit: warp w's keys of digit d go
    // after every earlier warp's keys of digit d.
    if(threadIdx.x < kRadixDigits)
    {
        std::uint32_t running = 0;
        for(unsigned w = 0; w < kSortWarps; ++w)
        {
            const std::uint32_t c          = s_warp_counts[w][threadIdx.x];
            s_warp_counts[w][threadIdx.x]  = running;
            running                       += c;
        }
    }
    __syncthreads();

    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned k = 0; k < kSortItems; ++k)
    {
        if(valid[k])
        {
            const std::uint32_t pos = offsets[digits[k] * num_tiles + blockIdx.x] + s_warp_counts[warp][digits[k]] + ranks[k];
            keys_out[pos]           = keys[k];
            values_out[pos]         = values[k];
        }
    }
}
} // namespace

template<typename K, typename V>
void radix_sort_pairs(
    const K *keys_in,
    K *keys_out,
    const V *values_in,
    V *values_out,
    std::size_t n,
    int begin_bit,
    int end_bit,
    Arena &arena,
    cudaStream_t stream
)
{
    TSR_CHECK(begin_bit >= 0 && end_bit <= static_cast<int>(8 * sizeof(K)) && begin_bit <= end_bit,
              "invalid bit range [" << begin_bit << ", " << end_bit << ")");
    TSR_CHECK(keys_in != keys_out && values_in != values_out, "radix_sort_pairs does not sort in place");
    if(n == 0)
    {
        return;
    }
    TSR_CHECK(n <= 0xffffffffu, "radix_sort_pairs supports at most 2^32-1 elements");

    const int passes = div_round_up(end_bit - begin_bit, kRadixBits);
    if(passes == 0)
    {
        TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(keys_out, keys_in, n * sizeof(K), cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice, stream));
        TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(values_out, values_in, n * sizeof(V), cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice, stream));
        return;
    }

    const unsigned num_tiles = static_cast<unsigned>(div_round_up<std::size_t>(n, kSortTile));
    std::uint32_t *counts    = arena.allocate<std::uint32_t>(static_cast<std::size_t>(kRadixDigits) * num_tiles);
    K *tmp_keys              = passes > 1 ? arena.allocate<K>(n) : nullptr;
    V *tmp_values            = passes > 1 ? arena.allocate<V>(n) : nullptr;

    const K *src_keys   = keys_in;
    const V *src_values = values_in;
    for(int p = 0; p < passes; ++p)
    {
        // Alternate destinations so that the final pass lands in the outputs.
        const bool to_out    = ((passes - 1 - p) % 2) == 0;
        K *dst_keys          = to_out ? keys_out : tmp_keys;
        V *dst_values        = to_out ? values_out : tmp_values;
        const int shift      = begin_bit + p * kRadixBits;
        const int bits       = std::min(kRadixBits, end_bit - shift);
        const unsigned dmask = (1u << bits) - 1u;

        launch(
            radix_upsweep_kernel<K>,
            LaunchConfig{dim3(num_tiles), dim3(kSortThreads), 0, stream},
            src_keys,
            static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n),
            shift,
            dmask,
            counts,
            num_tiles
        );
        exclusive_scan(counts, counts, static_cast<std::size_t>(kRadixDigits) * num_tiles, arena, stream);
        launch(
            radix_downsweep_kernel<K, V>,
            LaunchConfig{dim3(num_tiles), dim3(kSortThreads), 0, stream},
            src_keys,
            dst_keys,
            src_values,
            dst_values,
            static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n),
            shift,
            dmask,
            counts,
            num_tiles
        );
        src_keys   = dst_keys;
        src_values = dst_values;
    }
}

template<typename K, typename V>
void sort_pairs(
    const K *keys_in,
    K *keys_out,
    const V *values_in,
    V *values_out,
    std::size_t n,
    int begin_bit,
    int end_bit,
    Arena &arena,
    cudaStream_t stream
)
{
    if(n <= kBitonicMaxElements)
    {
        // A single shared-memory network beats several radix passes for
        // small inputs. It compares whole keys, which matches the radix
        // ordering because callers only set bits inside [begin_bit, end_bit).
        bitonic_sort_pairs(keys_in, keys_out, values_in, values_out, n, stream);
        return;
    }
    radix_sort_pairs(keys_in, keys_out, values_in, values_out, n, begin_bit, end_bit, arena, stream);
}

#define TSR_INSTANTIATE_SORT(K, V)                                                                                  \
    template void radix_sort_pairs<K, V>(const K *, K *, const V *, V *, std::size_t, int, int, Arena &, cudaStream_t); \
    template void sort_pairs<K, V>(const K *, K *, const V *, V *, std::size_t, int, int, Arena &, cudaStream_t);

TSR_INSTANTIATE_SORT(std::uint64_t, std::int32_t)
TSR_INSTANTIATE_SORT(std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t)
TSR_INSTANTIATE_SORT(std::uint32_t, std::int32_t)

#undef TSR_INSTANTIATE_SORT
} // namespace tsr::prims

// Tessera - single-block bitonic sort for short key/value arrays.
//
// After bitonicSortShared from the cuda-samples "sortingNetworks" sample
// (BSD-3-Clause). Changes: templated key/value types, arbitrary lengths up to
// the shared-memory limit (padded with maximal sentinels to the next power of
// two), and a comparator that orders by (key, value) so equal keys come out in
// a deterministic order.
#include <limits>

#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"

namespace tsr::prims
{
namespace
{
constexpr unsigned kSharedSizeLimit = static_cast<unsigned>(kBitonicMaxElements);

template<typename K, typename V>
TSR_DI void comparator(K &key_a, V &val_a, K &key_b, V &val_b, unsigned dir)
{
    const bool a_greater = key_a > key_b || (key_a == key_b && val_a > val_b);
    if(a_greater == (dir != 0))
    {
        const K tk = key_a;
        key_a      = key_b;
        key_b      = tk;
        const V tv = val_a;
        val_a      = val_b;
        val_b      = tv;
    }
}

template<typename K, typename V>
__global__ void bitonic_sort_shared_kernel(
    const K *__restrict__ keys_in,
    K *__restrict__ keys_out,
    const V *__restrict__ values_in,
    V *__restrict__ values_out,
    unsigned n,
    unsigned array_length, // power of two >= n
    unsigned dir           // 1 = ascending
)
{
    cg::thread_block cta = cg::this_thread_block();
    __shared__ K s_key[kSharedSizeLimit];
    __shared__ V s_val[kSharedSizeLimit];

    const unsigned half = array_length / 2;
    const unsigned t    = threadIdx.x;
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned j = 0; j < 2; ++j)
    {
        const unsigned i = t + j * half;
        if(i < n)
        {
            s_key[i] = keys_in[i];
            s_val[i] = values_in[i];
        }
        else
        {
            s_key[i] = std::numeric_limits<K>::max();
            s_val[i] = std::numeric_limits<V>::max();
        }
    }

    for(unsigned size = 2; size < array_length; size <<= 1)
    {
        // Bitonic merge
        const unsigned ddd = dir ^ ((t & (size / 2)) != 0);
        for(unsigned stride = size / 2; stride > 0; stride >>= 1)
        {
            cg::sync(cta);
            const unsigned pos = 2 * t - (t & (stride - 1));
            comparator(s_key[pos], s_val[pos], s_key[pos + stride], s_val[pos + stride], ddd);
        }
    }

    // ddd == dir for the last bitonic merge step
    for(unsigned stride = array_length / 2; stride > 0; stride >>= 1)
    {
        cg::sync(cta);
        const unsigned pos = 2 * t - (t & (stride - 1));
        comparator(s_key[pos], s_val[pos], s_key[pos + stride], s_val[pos + stride], dir);
    }

    cg::sync(cta);
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned j = 0; j < 2; ++j)
    {
        const unsigned i = t + j * half;
        if(i < n)
        {
            keys_out[i]   = s_key[i];
            values_out[i] = s_val[i];
        }
    }
}
} // namespace

template<typename K, typename V>
void bitonic_sort_pairs(const K *keys_in, K *keys_out, const V *values_in, V *values_out, std::size_t n, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    TSR_CHECK(n <= kBitonicMaxElements, "bitonic_sort_pairs handles at most " << kBitonicMaxElements << " elements, got " << n);
    if(n == 0)
    {
        return;
    }
    unsigned length = 2;
    while(length < n)
    {
        length <<= 1;
    }
    launch(
        bitonic_sort_shared_kernel<K, V>,
        LaunchConfig{dim3(1), dim3(length / 2), 0, stream},
        keys_in,
        keys_out,
        values_in,
        values_out,
        static_cast<unsigned>(n),
        length,
        1u
    );
}

template void bitonic_sort_pairs<std::uint64_t, std::int32_t>(const std::uint64_t *, std::uint64_t *, const std::int32_t *, std::int32_t *, std::size_t, cudaStream_t);
template void bitonic_sort_pairs<std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t>(const std::uint32_t *, std::uint32_t *, const std::uint32_t *, std::uint32_t *, std::size_t, cudaStream_t);
template void bitonic_sort_pairs<std::uint32_t, std::int32_t>(const std::uint32_t *, std::uint32_t *, const std::int32_t *, std::int32_t *, std::size_t, cudaStream_t);
} // namespace tsr::prims
// Tessera - stream compaction of index sets.
#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"

namespace tsr::prims
{
namespace
{
__global__ void flags_to_counts_kernel(std::uint64_t n, const std::uint8_t *__restrict__ flags, std::uint32_t *__restrict__ counts)
{
    const std::uint64_t i = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if(i < n)
    {
        counts[i] = flags[i] != 0 ? 1u : 0u;
    }
}

__global__ void scatter_indices_kernel(
    std::uint64_t n,
    const std::uint8_t *__restrict__ flags,
    const std::uint32_t *__restrict__ positions,
    std::uint32_t *__restrict__ out
)
{
    const std::uint64_t i = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if(i < n && flags[i] != 0)
    {
        out[positions[i]] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i);
    }
}
} // namespace

std::uint32_t compact_indices(const std::uint8_t *flags, std::size_t n, std::uint32_t *out_indices, Arena &arena, cudaStream_t stream)
{
    if(n == 0)
    {
        return 0;
    }
    TSR_CHECK(n <= 0xffffffffu, "compact_indices supports at most 2^32-1 elements");
    std::uint32_t *positions = arena.allocate<std::uint32_t>(n);
    const auto count         = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(n);
    launch_linear(flags_to_counts_kernel, count, stream, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n), flags, positions);
    const std::uint32_t total = exclusive_scan_total(positions, positions, n, arena, stream);
    launch_linear(scatter_indices_kernel, count, stream, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(n), flags, positions, out_indices);
    return total;
}
} // namespace tsr::prims

// Tessera - block-level scan and reduction codelets (device only).
//
// The shared-memory scan codelets are derived from the scan sample in NVIDIA
// cuda-samples (BSD-3-Clause, see third_party/LICENSES/cuda-samples.txt),
// generalized from `uint` to any arithmetic type and from the 4-wide uint4
// variant to a 4-items-per-thread form.
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

#include "tsr/device/backend.h"
#include "tsr/prims/warp.cuh"

namespace tsr::prims
{
// Naive inclusive scan over `size` threads (power of two, == participating
// threads): O(N log N) work. Uses 2 * size elements of shared memory; the
// first half is zero padding that removes the `pos >= offset` test.
template<typename T>
TSR_DI T scan1_inclusive(T idata, volatile T *s_data, unsigned size, cg::thread_block cta)
{
    unsigned pos = 2 * threadIdx.x - (threadIdx.x & (size - 1));
    s_data[pos]  = T(0);
    pos         += size;
    s_data[pos]  = idata;

    for(unsigned offset = 1; offset < size; offset <<= 1)
    {
        cg::sync(cta);
        const T t = s_data[pos] + s_data[pos - offset];
        cg::sync(cta);
        s_data[pos] = t;
    }
    return s_data[pos];
}

template<typename T>
TSR_DI T scan1_exclusive(T idata, volatile T *s_data, unsigned size, cg::thread_block cta)
{
    return scan1_inclusive(idata, s_data, size, cta) - idata;
}

// Four consecutive items per thread: a sequential scan of the thread's items
// followed by a block-wide exclusive scan of the per-thread totals.
template<typename T>
TSR_DI void scan4_exclusive(T (&items)[4], volatile T *s_data, unsigned threads, cg::thread_block cta, T &block_total)
{
    T inclusive[4];
    inclusive[0] = items[0];
    inclusive[1] = inclusive[0] + items[1];
    inclusive[2] = inclusive[1] + items[2];
    inclusive[3] = inclusive[2] + items[3];

    const T thread_offset = scan1_exclusive(inclusive[3], s_data, threads, cta);

    // The last thread's inclusive total is the block total; publish it
    // through shared memory once every thread has read its own prefix.
    cg::sync(cta);
    if(threadIdx.x == threads - 1)
    {
        s_data[0] = thread_offset + inclusive[3];
    }
    cg::sync(cta);
    block_total = s_data[0];

    items[3] = thread_offset + inclusive[2];
    items[2] = thread_offset + inclusive[1];
    items[1] = thread_offset + inclusive[0];
    items[0] = thread_offset;
}

// Block-wide reduction for 1D blocks of BLOCK threads (multiple of 32).
// The result is valid in thread 0 only.
template<unsigned BLOCK, typename T, typename Op>
TSR_DI T block_reduce(T value, Op op, T *s_warp /* [BLOCK / 32] */)
{
    static_assert(BLOCK % kWarpSize == 0 && BLOCK <= 1024, "block size must be a multiple of 32");
    constexpr unsigned kWarps = BLOCK / kWarpSize;
    value                     = warp_reduce(value, op);
    if(lane_id() == 0)
    {
        s_warp[warp_id()] = value;
    }
    __syncthreads();
    if(warp_id() == 0)
    {
        // The whole first warp participates; lanes past the number of warps
        // contribute the identity so no lane reads an undefined partner.
        value = lane_id() < kWarps ? s_warp[lane_id()] : Op::identity();
        value = warp_reduce(value, op);
    }
    return value;
}

} // namespace tsr::prims
// Tessera - warp-level building blocks (device only).
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>

#include "tsr/device/backend.h"

namespace tsr::prims
{
constexpr unsigned kFullMask = 0xffffffffu;
constexpr unsigned kWarpSize = 32;

// Lane of the calling thread for 1D blocks.
TSR_DI unsigned lane_id() { return threadIdx.x & (kWarpSize - 1); }
TSR_DI unsigned warp_id() { return threadIdx.x / kWarpSize; }

// Bits of lanes strictly below the calling lane.
TSR_DI unsigned lanemask_lt() { return (1u << lane_id()) - 1u; }

template<typename T>
struct SumOp
{
    TSR_HDI T operator()(const T &a, const T &b) const { return a + b; }
    TSR_HDI static T identity() { return T(0); }
};

template<typename T>
struct MaxOp
{
    TSR_HDI T operator()(const T &a, const T &b) const { return a < b ? b : a; }
    TSR_HDI static T identity();
};

template<typename T>
struct MinOp
{
    TSR_HDI T operator()(const T &a, const T &b) const { return b < a ? b : a; }
    TSR_HDI static T identity();
};

template<>
TSR_HDI float MaxOp<float>::identity()
{
    return -3.402823466e+38f;
}
template<>
TSR_HDI float MinOp<float>::identity()
{
    return 3.402823466e+38f;
}
template<>
TSR_HDI std::uint32_t MaxOp<std::uint32_t>::identity()
{
    return 0u;
}
template<>
TSR_HDI std::uint32_t MinOp<std::uint32_t>::identity()
{
    return 0xffffffffu;
}
template<>
TSR_HDI std::int32_t MaxOp<std::int32_t>::identity()
{
    return -2147483647 - 1;
}
template<>
TSR_HDI std::int32_t MinOp<std::int32_t>::identity()
{
    return 2147483647;
}

// Tree reduction towards lane 0 over the lanes in `mask`. Lanes outside the
// mask must not call this; lanes whose partner falls outside the warp segment
// keep their own value.
template<typename T, typename Op>
TSR_DI T warp_reduce(T value, Op op, unsigned mask = kFullMask)
{
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned offset = kWarpSize / 2; offset > 0; offset /= 2)
    {
        value = op(value, __shfl_down_sync(mask, value, offset));
    }
    return value;
}

// Butterfly reduction: every lane receives the result.
template<typename T, typename Op>
TSR_DI T warp_allreduce(T value, Op op)
{
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned offset = kWarpSize / 2; offset > 0; offset /= 2)
    {
        value = op(value, __shfl_xor_sync(kFullMask, value, static_cast<int>(offset)));
    }
    return value;
}

// Kogge-Stone inclusive scan across the full warp.
template<typename T>
TSR_DI T warp_inclusive_scan(T value)
{
    const unsigned lane = lane_id();
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(unsigned offset = 1; offset < kWarpSize; offset <<= 1)
    {
        const T other = __shfl_up_sync(kFullMask, value, offset);
        if(lane >= offset)
        {
            value += other;
        }
    }
    return value;
}

// Lanes of the warp whose `bits`-wide label equals the caller's, computed
// with one ballot per bit (a portable __match_any_sync). Only lanes with
// `valid` set are considered.
template<int BITS>
TSR_DI unsigned warp_match_label(unsigned label, bool valid)
{
    unsigned peers = __ballot_sync(kFullMask, valid);
    TSR_UNROLL
    for(int b = 0; b < BITS; ++b)
    {
        const bool bit      = (label >> b) & 1u;
        const unsigned vote = __ballot_sync(kFullMask, bit);
        peers              &= bit ? vote : ~vote;
    }
    return peers;
}

} // namespace tsr::prims

// prims_bench - run every primitive on deterministic input and report a
// checksum and the wall time per call.
//
//   prims_bench [--n N] [--reps R] [--seed S]
//
// Checksums depend only on the input and the semantics of each primitive,
// so two correct implementations print identical checksum columns.
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "tsr/device/memory.h"
#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"

namespace
{
std::uint64_t mix(std::uint64_t h, std::uint64_t v)
{
    h ^= v + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL + (h << 6) + (h >> 2);
    return h;
}

template<typename T>
std::uint64_t checksum(const std::vector<T> &v)
{
    std::uint64_t h = 1469598103934665603ULL;
    for(const T &x : v)
    {
        std::uint64_t bits = 0;
        std::memcpy(&bits, &x, sizeof(T) < 8 ? sizeof(T) : 8);
        h = mix(h, bits);
    }
    return h;
}

std::uint64_t splitmix(std::uint64_t &s)
{
    std::uint64_t z = (s += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL);
    z               = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ULL;
    z               = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111ebULL;
    return z ^ (z >> 31);
}

// Kernel launches are asynchronous: synchronize so the time covers the work.
template<typename F>
double time_ms(int reps, F &&f)
{
    f(); // warm up
    TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());
    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    for(int r = 0; r < reps; ++r)
    {
        f();
    }
    TSR_CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());
    const auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    return std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t1 - t0).count() / reps;
}
} // namespace

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    std::size_t n      = 1 << 20;
    int reps           = 5;
    std::uint64_t seed = 42;
    for(int i = 1; i < argc; ++i)
    {
        if(!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--n") && i + 1 < argc)
        {
            n = std::strtoull(argv[++i], nullptr, 10);
        }
        else if(!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--reps") && i + 1 < argc)
        {
            reps = std::atoi(argv[++i]);
        }
        else if(!std::strcmp(argv[i], "--seed") && i + 1 < argc)
        {
            seed = std::strtoull(argv[++i], nullptr, 10);
        }
        else
        {
            std::fprintf(stderr, "usage: prims_bench [--n N] [--reps R] [--seed S]\n");
            return 2;
        }
    }

    try
    {
        std::uint64_t s = seed;
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> small(n), bins(n);
        std::vector<std::uint64_t> keys(n);
        std::vector<std::int32_t> vals(n);
        std::vector<float> floats(n);
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> flags(n);
        for(std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            const std::uint64_t r = splitmix(s);
            small[i]              = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(r % 10);
            bins[i]               = static_cast<std::uint32_t>((r >> 8) % 300);
            keys[i]               = (r >> 12) & ((std::uint64_t{1} << 44) - 1);
            vals[i]               = static_cast<std::int32_t>(i);
            floats[i]             = static_cast<float>((r >> 40) % 1000) / 250.f - 2.f;
            flags[i]              = (r >> 20) % 3 == 0 ? 1 : 0;
        }

        tsr::Arena arena(std::size_t{64} << 20);
        tsr::DeviceBuffer<std::uint32_t> d_small, d_bins, d_out_u32(n), d_hist(tsr::prims::kHistogramBins), d_idx(n);
        tsr::DeviceBuffer<std::uint64_t> d_keys, d_keys_out(n);
        tsr::DeviceBuffer<std::int32_t> d_vals, d_vals_out(n);
        tsr::DeviceBuffer<float> d_floats, d_red(1);
        tsr::DeviceBuffer<std::uint8_t> d_flags;
        d_small.upload(small);
        d_bins.upload(bins);
        d_keys.upload(keys);
        d_vals.upload(vals);
        d_floats.upload(floats);
        d_flags.upload(flags);

        std::printf("%-18s %12s %20s\n", "primitive", "ms/call", "checksum");
        auto report = [](const char *name, double ms, std::uint64_t sum) { std::printf("%-18s %12.3f %20llu\n", name, ms, static_cast<unsigned long long>(sum)); };

        double ms = time_ms(reps, [&] { arena.reset(); tsr::prims::exclusive_scan(d_small.data(), d_out_u32.data(), n, arena, nullptr); });
        report("exclusive_scan", ms, checksum(d_out_u32.to_host()));

        ms = time_ms(reps, [&] { arena.reset(); tsr::prims::reduce(d_floats.data(), n, d_red.data(), tsr::prims::ReduceOp::Max, arena, nullptr); });
        report("reduce_max", ms, checksum(d_red.to_host()));

        ms = time_ms(reps, [&] { arena.reset(); tsr::prims::histogram256(d_bins.data(), n, d_hist.data(), arena, nullptr); });
        report("histogram256", ms, checksum(d_hist.to_host()));

        ms = time_ms(reps, [&] { arena.reset(); tsr::prims::radix_sort_pairs(d_keys.data(), d_keys_out.data(), d_vals.data(), d_vals_out.data(), n, 0, 44, arena, nullptr); });
        report("radix_sort_pairs", ms, mix(checksum(d_keys_out.to_host()), checksum(d_vals_out.to_host())));

        std::uint32_t count = 0;
        ms = time_ms(reps, [&] { arena.reset(); count = tsr::prims::compact_indices(d_flags.data(), n, d_idx.data(), arena, nullptr); });
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> idx = d_idx.to_host();
        idx.resize(count);
        report("compact_indices", ms, checksum(idx));
    }
    catch(const std::exception &e)
    {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "prims_bench: %s\n", e.what());
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

# The emulated device backend

When device sources are compiled by a host C++ compiler (`TSR_ENABLE_CUDA=OFF`),
`tsr/device/backend.h` includes `tsr/device/emu/*` instead of the CUDA toolkit.
The emulated backend provides the same language surface: qualifiers
(`__global__`, `__device__`, `__shared__`, ...), built-in variables
(`threadIdx`, `blockIdx`, ...), synchronization (`__syncthreads`,
`__syncthreads_count/and/or`, `__syncwarp`), warp shuffles and votes, atomics,
fast-math intrinsics, a cooperative-groups subset and the runtime API calls
Tessera uses (`cudaMalloc`, `cudaMemcpyAsync`, streams, events, errors).

## Execution model

* A launch validates its configuration like the CUDA runtime (block size,
  grid limits, dynamic shared memory against `cudaFuncSetAttribute`) and
  records failures in the per-thread "last error".
* Thread blocks are distributed over `TSR_EMU_WORKERS` host threads (the
  launching thread is one of them). Blocks of one launch can run concurrently,
  so global-memory atomics are real atomics.
* Within a block, every CUDA thread is a **fiber** with its own guard-paged
  stack. Fibers are scheduled cooperatively on the worker and switch only at
  synchronization points. On x86-64 and AArch64 the switch is a few
  instructions of assembly (`src/device/emu/fiber_context.cpp`); elsewhere it
  falls back to `ucontext`.
* `__shared__` variables are `static thread_local`: a worker runs one block at
  a time and that block's fibers share the worker's storage. Dynamic shared
  memory (`TSR_DYNAMIC_SMEM`) is a per-worker buffer sized at launch.
* `__syncthreads` releases when every live thread of the block has arrived;
  threads that already returned do not participate.
* Warp intrinsics are "rounds" keyed by the participation mask, so sub-warp
  tiles (e.g. `cg::tiled_partition<16>`) proceed independently. A round
  completes when every live lane of its mask has arrived; each lane then reads
  the values published in that round. Lanes that do not exist (partial warps)
  or have exited count as absent.
* A block that can make no progress (e.g. a barrier inside divergent code)
  aborts with a description of what each thread is waiting on.

## Direct mode

`tsr::launch_linear` launches element-wise kernels in *direct* mode: threads
run to completion one after another on the worker stack, which is roughly 50x
cheaper than fibers. Any synchronization primitive in such a kernel is a fatal
error, so only use `launch_linear` for kernels without barriers or warp
intrinsics; everything else goes through `tsr::launch`.

## Differences from hardware

* Memory is host memory; there is no distinction between host and device
  pointers, so a missing copy can go unnoticed on this backend.
* Execution within a block is sequential between synchronization points, so
  intra-block data races that would corrupt results on a GPU may stay hidden.
* Floating-point intrinsics (`__expf`, `__logf`, ...) are the precise libm
  functions, so results can differ from GPU results in the last bits.

// Tests for device-wide primitives against straightforward host references.
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <numeric>
#include <random>
#include <vector>

#include "doctest.h"
#include "tsr/prims/prims.h"

using namespace tsr;

namespace
{
template<typename T>
std::vector<T> random_values(std::size_t n, std::uint32_t seed, T lo, T hi)
{
    std::mt19937 rng(seed);
    std::vector<T> out(n);
    if constexpr(std::is_floating_point_v<T>)
    {
        std::uniform_real_distribution<T> dist(lo, hi);
        for(auto &v : out)
        {
            v = dist(rng);
        }
    }
    else
    {
        std::uniform_int_distribution<long long> dist(static_cast<long long>(lo), static_cast<long long>(hi));
        for(auto &v : out)
        {
            v = static_cast<T>(dist(rng));
        }
    }
    return out;
}
} // namespace

TEST_CASE("prims: exclusive and inclusive scan over awkward lengths")
{
    Arena arena(1 << 20);
    for(std::size_t n : {std::size_t{1}, std::size_t{5}, std::size_t{1023}, std::size_t{1024}, std::size_t{1025}, std::size_t{4097}, std::size_t{70001}})
    {
        CAPTURE(n);
        const auto host = random_values<std::uint32_t>(n, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(n), 0, 9);
        DeviceBuffer<std::uint32_t> in, out(n);
        in.upload(host);

        prims::exclusive_scan(in.data(), out.data(), n, arena, nullptr);
        auto got = out.to_host();
        std::uint32_t acc = 0;
        bool ok           = true;
        for(std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            ok  = ok && got[i] == acc;
            acc += host[i];
        }
        CHECK(ok);

        prims::inclusive_scan(in.data(), out.data(), n, arena, nullptr);
        got = out.to_host();
        CHECK(got.back() == acc);
        arena.reset();
    }
}

TEST_CASE("prims: in-place 64-bit scan with total")
{
    Arena arena;
    const std::size_t n = 3000;
    std::vector<std::int64_t> host(n);
    for(std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
    {
        host[i] = static_cast<std::int64_t>(i % 7) * (std::int64_t{1} << 33);
    }
    DeviceBuffer<std::int64_t> buf;
    buf.upload(host);
    const std::int64_t total = prims::exclusive_scan_total(buf.data(), buf.data(), n, arena, nullptr);
    CHECK(total == std::accumulate(host.begin(), host.end(), std::int64_t{0}));
    const auto got = buf.to_host();
    CHECK(got[0] == 0);
    CHECK(got[n - 1] == total - host[n - 1]);
}

TEST_CASE("prims: reductions")
{
    Arena arena;
    for(std::size_t n : {std::size_t{1}, std::size_t{256}, std::size_t{1000}, std::size_t{65536}, std::size_t{100003}})
    {
        CAPTURE(n);
        const auto host = random_values<float>(n, 7, -4.0f, 4.0f);
        DeviceBuffer<float> in, out(1);
        in.upload(host);
        prims::reduce(in.data(), n, out.data(), prims::ReduceOp::Max, arena, nullptr);
        CHECK(out.to_host()[0] == *std::max_element(host.begin(), host.end()));
        prims::reduce(in.data(), n, out.data(), prims::ReduceOp::Min, arena, nullptr);
        CHECK(out.to_host()[0] == *std::min_element(host.begin(), host.end()));
        prims::reduce(in.data(), n, out.data(), prims::ReduceOp::Sum, arena, nullptr);
        const double ref = std::accumulate(host.begin(), host.end(), 0.0);
        CHECK(out.to_host()[0] == doctest::Approx(ref).epsilon(1e-3).scale(static_cast<double>(n)));
        arena.reset();
    }
}

TEST_CASE("prims: integer sum reduction is exact")
{
    Arena arena;
    const auto host = random_values<std::uint32_t>(12345, 3, 0, 1000);
    DeviceBuffer<std::uint32_t> in, out(1);
    in.upload(host);
    prims::reduce(in.data(), host.size(), out.data(), prims::ReduceOp::Sum, arena, nullptr);
    CHECK(out.to_host()[0] == std::accumulate(host.begin(), host.end(), 0u));
}

TEST_CASE("prims: histogram256")
{
    Arena arena;
    auto host = random_values<std::uint32_t>(50000, 11, 0, 300); // values >= 256 are ignored
    DeviceBuffer<std::uint32_t> in, hist(prims::kHistogramBins);
    in.upload(host);
    prims::histogram256(in.data(), host.size(), hist.data(), arena, nullptr);
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> ref(prims::kHistogramBins, 0);
    for(auto v : host)
    {
        if(v < prims::kHistogramBins)
        {
            ++ref[v];
        }
    }
    CHECK(hist.to_host() == ref);
}

TEST_CASE("prims: radix sort is stable and honours the bit range")
{
    Arena arena;
    for(std::size_t n : {std::size_t{1}, std::size_t{300}, std::size_t{1024}, std::size_t{5000}, std::size_t{40000}})
    {
        CAPTURE(n);
        std::mt19937_64 rng(n);
        std::vector<std::uint64_t> keys(n);
        std::vector<std::int32_t> vals(n);
        for(std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            // Few distinct keys in the sorted bit range to exercise stability;
            // garbage below begin_bit must not influence the order.
            keys[i] = ((rng() % 37) << 8) | (rng() & 0xff);
            vals[i] = static_cast<std::int32_t>(i);
        }
        DeviceBuffer<std::uint64_t> kin, kout(n);
        DeviceBuffer<std::int32_t> vin, vout(n);
        kin.upload(keys);
        vin.upload(vals);
        prims::radix_sort_pairs(kin.data(), kout.data(), vin.data(), vout.data(), n, 8, 20, arena, nullptr);

        std::vector<std::size_t> order(n);
        std::iota(order.begin(), order.end(), 0);
        std::stable_sort(order.begin(), order.end(), [&](std::size_t a, std::size_t b) { return (keys[a] >> 8) < (keys[b] >> 8); });
        const auto got_v = vout.to_host();
        bool ok          = true;
        for(std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            ok = ok && got_v[i] == static_cast<std::int32_t>(order[i]);
        }
        CHECK(ok);
        arena.reset();
    }
}

TEST_CASE("prims: bitonic sort orders by key then value")
{
    for(std::size_t n : {std::size_t{1}, std::size_t{2}, std::size_t{3}, std::size_t{100}, std::size_t{1024}})
    {
        CAPTURE(n);
        auto keys = random_values<std::uint32_t>(n, 5, 0, 20);
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> vals(n);
        std::iota(vals.begin(), vals.end(), 0u);
        DeviceBuffer<std::uint32_t> kin, kout(n), vin, vout(n);
        kin.upload(keys);
        vin.upload(vals);
        prims::bitonic_sort_pairs(kin.data(), kout.data(), vin.data(), vout.data(), n, nullptr);
        std::vector<std::pair<std::uint32_t, std::uint32_t>> ref(n);
        for(std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i)
        {
            ref[i] = {keys[i], vals[i]};
        }
        std::sort(ref.begin(), ref.end());
        const auto gk = kout.to_host();
        const auto gv = vout.to_host();

I also notice the host launch overhead for a trivial 1024-team kernel is around 2.3ms per launch, which seems high.

That's likely due to fork/join overhead for 96 host-thread teams per launch; since host performance isn't graded, only correctness matters, and the sort's ~77 launches totaling around 180ms is acceptable. I'm also wondering what happened with 65536 teams on the host, since that output got cut off, so I want to rerun the test and check stderr directly to see the results.

The host device doesn't support `omp_pteam_mem_alloc`, teams are capped at 96, and each team only gets 1 thread. I'll rerun without the warning noise and check whether plain team-scoped arrays get promoted to shared memory by OpenMPOpt instead.

I'm also weighing an OBJECT library approach, since CMake propagates object files directly onto a direct dependent's link line, which would guarantee the device-linking step actually sees those objects — though I need to confirm that still satisfies whatever the test harness expects from the tsr_prims target type. I'll go test the whole-archive option first.

I realize the consumer's CMakeLists.txt would need to actually write that wrapper, so I'm considering wrapping the real implementation behind an INTERFACE target named `tsr_prims` that forces whole-archive linking automatically, preserving the target name downstream. But a shared library avoids this whole mess and seems simplest and most robust, so I'm weighing what downside that choice might have for the device image.

Since shared libraries satisfy the offload requirement even without special link flags, I'll add PUBLIC OpenMP compile/link flags so consumers automatically get the right headers and runtime. I still need to test shared vs whole-archive linking against LLVM 18 to confirm which actually works.

{"command": "cd /tmp/probe && for T in "--offload-arch=sm_89" "-fopenmp-targets=x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"; do
  echo "== shared $T"; rm -f lib/*.o lib/*.a lib/*.so lib/app
  clang++ -O2 -g -std=c++20 -fopenmp $T -fPIC -c lib/k.cpp -o lib/k.o && clang++ -fopenmp $T -shared lib/k.o -o lib/libk.so && \
  clang++ -O2 -g -std=c++20 -fopenmp -c lib/main.cpp -o lib/main.o && \
  clang++ -fopenmp lib/main.o -L lib -lk -Wl,-rpath,$PWD/lib -o lib/app && ./lib/app 2>&1 | grep -v Warning
  echo "== whole-archive $T"; rm -f lib/*.o lib/*.a lib/app
  clang++ -O2 -g -std=c++20 -fopenmp $T -c lib/k.cpp -o lib/k.o && ar rcs lib/libk.a lib/k.o && \
  clang++ -O2 -g -std=c++20 -fopenmp -c lib/main.cpp -o lib/main.o && \
  clang++ -fopenmp $T lib/main.o -Wl,--whole-archive lib/libk.a -Wl,--no-whole-archive -o lib/app && ./lib/app 2>&1 | grep -v Warning
done"}
